one_line_thesis: Leading CAPP met coal producer with deep reserves and net cash, but FY2025 buybacks ($1.14B) far exceeded trough owner cash ($145M OCF); normalized component economics (~$63/sh) sit far below price (~$153).

deep_dive.executive_summary: Alpha Metallurgical Resources is the largest U.S. exporter of metallurgical coal from Central Appalachia, with 294.5 million tons of reserves and $436 million of net cash at June 2026. FY2025 was a cycle trough: net loss $62 million, operating cash flow $145 million, yet the company repurchased $1.14 billion of stock. H1 2026 shows partial recovery but not a full mid-cycle run-rate. At $169.44, our trough-to-midcycle owner-cash model implies about -11.57% per year over seven years, and filing-normalized component economics near $63 per share sit far below price. industry.structure: U.S. metallurgical coal is an oligopoly of low-cost CAPP and Alabama longwall producers selling into seaborne steel markets; Alpha is among the largest U.S. met exporters with port capacity and reserve depth.
industry.share_shift: Alpha gained scale via the 2018 ANR merger and has shrunk the share count by roughly one-third since 2022 through repurchases, while industry supply responds to Chinese and Indian steel demand and Australian export competition.
industry.trend: Met coal prices collapsed from 2022 peaks through 2025, pushing Alpha into a net loss year while management continued aggressive buybacks; H1 2026 shows partial revenue recovery but earnings remain negative.
